title: Make room
hook: when told to make room in assemblies, make room, and Allah makes room for you (58:11)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Mujadila, and your line was she was heard. Did you say your calm sentence, and how was it received? Day six hundred seventeen.

A crowded table at a family dinner. Someone arrives late, plate in hand, and stands there. Everyone is mid-conversation. Nobody moves. The latecomer hovers, then drifts toward the kitchen counter to eat alone. It takes one person to say, here, squeeze in, and shift their chair six inches. Six inches, and someone belongs. Surah Al-Mujadila has a verse about exactly that moment, set in the gatherings around the Prophet ﷺ in Medina. And it comes with a promise attached.

Verse eleven. Pickthall: "O ye who believe! when it is said, Make room! in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make way for you (hereafter)." The Arabic verb is tafassahu, make space, spread out, from the root f-s-h, wideness, roominess. Commentators report the setting: people were sitting close around the Prophet, and some who'd come late, among them men who had fought at Badr, were left standing, because those already seated didn't want to give up their places near him. The verse answers: make room. And notice the trade. You give up a few inches, and God makes room for you. Commentators read that widely: room in the grave, room in paradise, room in your life and your heart, room in your provision. The verse continues: and when you're told to rise, rise; God will raise those of you who believe, and those given knowledge, by degrees. Hadith fill in the manners. Bukhari and Muslim record that the Prophet said no one should make another person get up from his seat so that he can sit there. Instead, spread out and make room. So the rule cuts both ways. The one sitting should shift and make space. The one arriving shouldn't push anyone out. Between them, a crowded room gets bigger without a single chair being added. In this verse, space isn't only something you have. It's something people make for each other.
screen: `TAFASSAHU: MAKE SPACE.` · `LATECOMERS LEFT STANDING.` · `MAKE ROOM, AND GOD MAKES ROOM.` · `DON'T MAKE ANYONE GET UP.`

segments.voice: The practice: make space for someone. Sit, and notice how much room you take up right now: your arms, your legs, your bag. Breathe in, and feel yourself settle. Breathe out, and shift slightly, as if leaving a space beside you. Now think of one person who's been standing at the edge of something: a new coworker, a quiet cousin, a neighbor. Picture moving your chair six inches for them. The bell holds the time.
Make room. When told to make room in gatherings, make room, and God will make room for you. Today's word.
Your line: squeeze in, shift six inches. Today, at a table, a meeting or a group chat, make literal or figurative room for one person who's on the edge. Day six hundred seventeen.

howItsDone: In mosques and gatherings, Muslims are taught to close up and make room for newcomers, especially in the rows of prayer and at the Friday sermon, and not to make anyone rise from their seat.

fork.setup: you're seated near the Prophet. latecomers, including men who fought at Badr, are standing with nowhere to sit. what does the verse say?
options: ask them to come back later.
fork.reveal: commentators place the verse here: make room, and God will make room for you.

original.note: Arabic: make room in the gatherings. majalis are sittings, assemblies.

trapdoor: what you thought: a verse about seating manners.
what it means: a few inches given, and God makes room in return, in this life and the next.
what a scholar hears: tafassahu from f-s-h; the occasion reported with the people of Badr; 'yafsahi llahu lakum' read broadly; Bukhari 6270 and Muslim 2177 on not raising anyone from his seat.
